answer: One concrete defence is a time-locked stake vault: a new identity must lock a deposit that only unlocks after sustained useful work, so spawning accounts is cheap but making any of them influential is slow and expensive. Random peer juries grade the work, and collusion triggers slashing of the whole stake. A tide of fake identities therefore cannot buy standing in bulk — each must earn it separately. A jade mark of reputation, granted only after repeated verified contributions, lets others trust proven history while every newcomer still starts at zero.
